title: Algebraic criteria for complete relaxation in autonomous and periodically driven open quantum systems
abstract: We derive sufficient criteria that guarantee convergence of open quantum system dynamics to a unique long-time state independent of the initial conditions. We refer to this behavior as complete relaxation. Focusing on systems described by Gorini-Kossakowski-Sudarshan-Lindblad (GKSL) master equations on finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, our approach uses only elementary mathematical arguments. For autonomous systems, we recover three previously derived relaxation criteria, which can be expressed as algebraic conditions on the Lindblad operators and the Hamiltonian entering the GKSL equation. For periodically driven systems, we obtain a new criterion involving a similar algebraic condition and a local continuity requirement on the time-dependent GKSL generator. This result implies an earlier criterion for complete relaxation formulated in Ref. [J. Phys. A 52, 43LT01 (2019)]. We also discuss implications of our approach for periodically modulated classical master equations, as well as extensions to driven systems without a periodicity constraint.
summary: This paper develops algebraic criteria to determine when an open quantum system, governed by the GKSL master equation, achieves 'complete relaxation' to a unique steady state. It provides simplified, verifiable conditions for both time-independent and periodically driven systems. The results are significant for understanding the long-time dynamics of quantum processes in physics.
main_problem: The paper aims to derive sufficient, elementary mathematical criteria that guarantee 'complete relaxation' in open quantum systems, meaning the system converges to a unique long-time state regardless of its initial conditions.
main_result: For periodically driven systems, a new criterion is established: complete relaxation is guaranteed if an algebraic condition on the Lindblad operators is met at any single instant within the driving period, provided the generator is continuous.
method: The approach relies on analyzing the algebraic structure (using the concept of the algebra generated by operators) of the Lindblad operators and the Hamiltonian within the Gorini-Kossakowski-Sudarshan-Lindblad (GKSL) master equation framework.
model_or_system: The study focuses on open quantum systems modeled by the GKSL master equation, applicable to both autonomous (time-independent) and periodically driven systems on finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces. The dynamics are governed by the time-dependent Lindblad generator.
key_observables: Complete relaxation (convergence to a unique long-time state), the spectral range of associated operators, and the algebraic structure of the Lindblad operators.
important_parameters: The driving period $T$ (for periodic systems), the Lindblad operators $A_\mu$, and the Hamiltonian $\hat{H}_t$.
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces. The criterion for periodic driving is sufficient, and the general time-dependent case requires analyzing the full dynamical map.
figures_summary: Figure 1 provides an overview illustrating the interdependencies between the derived theorems based on whether the generator is time-independent, periodic, or arbitrarily time-dependent.
paper_structure: The paper systematically develops criteria for relaxation, first addressing the autonomous case with algebraic conditions on the Lindblad operators. It then extends these results to the periodically driven case, yielding a simplified criterion, and finally discusses the more complex requirements for general time-dependent driving.
why_interesting: This work provides powerful, purely algebraic tools to diagnose the long-term behavior of complex open quantum systems, which is crucial for understanding thermalization, quantum computing decoherence, and quantum thermodynamics.
